added_failure_derivation: Read from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite logs (68 passed / 74 passed with EXIT=0 and no FAILED lines at either revision), so the failing-id sets are both empty and their difference is empty. The importer arm's base and head id files diff identical (9 failed each). The instrument is shown able to see a failure present: negative-control-base.log, produced by the same runner on the same test file, records 6 FAILED ids and EXIT=1, so the empty failure list is a measured zero rather than a silent one.

assertion_audit.fails_if: Dropping carried_program from the recipe (KeyError), omitting source/version, or failing to strip the value fails; the path and checksum sides are the values the test itself handed to compose, so they hold for any pass-through and would not redden a stuck resolver or a dropped sha256: prefix.
Deleting the carried-directory seal makes _mount_index raise 'no --ro-bind of ... in argv', so the ordering guard reddens on exactly the mounted-grant regression it was added for.
Removing the carried substitution leaves the task refusing with NOT_STARTED and the marker unwritten.

assertion_audit.assertion: recorded in result.stderr and sha256(program bytes) in result.stderr and not marker.exists()
assertion_audit.fails_if: Removing the digest comparison runs the task (entrypoint 0, marker written) and prints no checksums; the recorded 64-zero digest and the file's own digest are two independently derived values.

assertion_audit.assertion: str(absent) in result.stderr and not marker.exists()
assertion_audit.fails_if: Falling back to a path search or refusing without naming the carried location leaves the marker written or the path absent from the message.

assertion_audit.assertion: result.returncode == 0 and "Read-only file system" in result.stderr and program.read_bytes() == original
assertion_audit.fails_if: Removing the carried-directory seal lets the task replace the program (exit 9) and create a sibling directory (exit 8); the bytes are compared against a snapshot read before the task ran.

assertion_independence: One assertion is not independent of its input: tests/test_a_job_fence_starts_on_any_node.py:474 compares the recipe's path and checksum against the same values the test passed to compose, so it is a pass-through check rather than a resolution check. The durability of this change does not rest on it — :483, :538, :560 and :587 each name the regression they redden on. No added assertion covers the sha256: prefix handling that _checksum_text and the bootstrap's _checksum exist for.
evidence_limits: No suite re-run: the recorded completed arms and their EXIT=0 summary lines were read instead.
No scheduler job re-run: the two receipts under measure-run/ were read; the betelgeuse job's system_fence_program=false is what shows only the carried copy could have fenced it.
The s14 negative control names a betelgeuse job at the base revision; only a local pytest base arm exists, so the base job refusal is inferred from section s12's landed behaviour.

The carried program's flight key is not declared in reckon/schema/flight.yaml, so strict flight validation refuses it today; see the outside_scope entry in the reviewed manifest and the finding below.

findings.text: non-blocking: carried_fence_program resolves its flight path with an inline home-relative rule that duplicates the module's existing owner _resolve_declared_path at reckon/_worker_fence.py:1263 instead of calling it; the two disagree on the ~user form, which Path.expanduser resolves and the new rule treats as relative, so two flight keys written with the same path syntax resolve to different locations — fold the call into _resolve_declared_path.

non-blocking: the equality assertion compares the recipe's path, checksum, source and version against the same values the test handed to compose through _carried_recipe, so it holds for any pass-through and would survive a resolver regression; the guard that carries this test is the mount-order assertion at :483, and a case supplying a sha256:-prefixed checksum and a ~/-relative path would give the assertion an independent side.

non-blocking: _checksum_text's documented purpose — accepting the sha256:-prefixed spelling beside bare hex — is asserted by no added case; every new test supplies a bare digest, so replacing the prefix strip with plain str() leaves the suite green, and the mirrored _checksum at reckon/nested_launch.py:531 is equally unexercised in the prefixed spelling.

non-blocking: the flight schema declares no top-level fence_program key, so reckon flight --check in strict mode refuses the composition this node makes runnable and the deliverable's 'a location the flight settings name' has no declared home; the reviewed manifest declares this under outside_scope, and declaring it means editing the LinkML source and regenerating reckon/_flight_schema.py in a follow-up node.

non-blocking: s14's done_when asks for the base-revision negative control to be the betelgeuse job refusing with s12's message; the record substitutes a local pytest arm (6 failed at 57235c8, EXIT=1), so the base behaviour on a node holding no fence program is inherited from section s12 rather than measured for this section.
